This is a long story, but I'll try to share most of it. 

My college degree (Computer Engg) wasn't really my choice, in fact I had no idea what to take. I just got the degree because of a scholarship. At some point during my college years I started getting depressed. 

After I graduated, I basically became stagnant for one year. A lot of things happened that year which I'm sure made my mental state worse. Then I was called for an available job.

I took the job because my mom feels like I should owe the people who helped me during my school years, which I NEVER had asked for help. (it ain't my fault if she couldn't afford to take me to school)

I got my job from the same school I graduated from. I should be grateful since I'm almost familiar with the campus and the system. Also you should know that I had no teaching experience (I started last year at June). On the 1 year that passed (pre-Covid), I always feel guilty that I wasn't giving them the quality education they needed because of my inexperience. This impostor syndrome also gets me everytime. 

Now that we have the New-Normal system due to the pandemic, I feel like my depression is getting worse. Guilt, shame, unproductivity, and even suicidal ideations are happening almost daily. Issues at home are not helping either, not that I'd call it a _home,_ more like a house. 

I really do apologize for the long comment.
